### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **27** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**18** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 21ad7c540df659f5757a0a023ebb7e6cbf281bb3`.

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 21ad7c540df659f5757a0a023ebb7e6cbf281bb3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c8da9715a945ea200e64b59e8789c5fc738d4918` — the merge of head `07fe4d2fa8773b97ee53443707e5fe37c20501de` into base `21ad7c540df659f5757a0a023ebb7e6cbf281bb3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c8da9715a945ea200e64b59e8789c5fc738d4918 && git checkout c8da9715a945ea200e64b59e8789c5fc738d4918
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 21ad7c540df659f5757a0a023ebb7e6cbf281bb3 07fe4d2fa8773b97ee53443707e5fe37c20501de && git checkout -B drift-repro 21ad7c540df659f5757a0a023ebb7e6cbf281bb3 && git merge --no-ff 07fe4d2fa8773b97ee53443707e5fe37c20501de

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 21ad7c540df659f5757a0a023ebb7e6cbf281bb3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 21ad7c540df659f5757a0a023ebb7e6cbf281bb3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `07fe4d2fa8773b97ee53443707e5fe37c20501de`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json,packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/grade.ts + packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/cases.ts,packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/run.ts,packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/summary.ts,packages/qa/scenarios/src/skill-evals/self-test.ts,packages/qa/scenarios/README.md
Security-touching: yes

Read for this record: card #37928 (body, triage 7218032083, claim 7218758112, dev report 7219513608), PR #37969 (body, 8 files, head comment 7220004173), the net diff against `main` (merge-base `bc173343ea`), the 50 check-runs on the head (34 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed), and the 40 recorded turns of rounds A and B under `/mnt/project-files/epic-36996/37928/`, read as data. Nothing was built, tested or re-run; the recorded answers were re-read with a plain literal substring count, not the runner. The scratch driver is not in the repository and was not read.

### ① Derived judgments

- `parseEvalFile` accepts one new key, `assertions.must_contain_any`. On `main` the key was silently ignored (a case carrying only it refused as asserting nothing). Now it is read, enforced and refused when malformed. Right.
- A case that asserts only groups is read (`rawMc.length + rawMnc.length + groups.length === 0` is the only asserts-nothing refusal). Right, and case 6 keeps a `must_not_contain` beside its group anyway.
- `GradeResult.unmetAny`, `Verdict.unmetAny` and `SkillEvalRunRecord.unmetAny` are optional and written only when a group is unmet, so a grade result and a run record of a case without the form keep their old shape. `RUN_RECORD_SCHEMA` stays `skill-eval-run/1`: an additive optional key, right.
- `CaseScore.withSkillUnmetAny` is a required key, so `round.json` gains `"withSkillUnmetAny": []` on every behaviour case, with or without the form (round A's `round.json` shows it on main's tokens). Additive; its only readers in the tree are `summary.ts` and the suite, which reads fields, and the suite is green on the head. Right. The PR body's "byte-identical" claim is true of the grade result and the run record, which is what it says.
- `hashCase` adds `mustContainAny` to `extra` only when the list is non-empty, after `shouldTrigger` and `files`, and leaves `parts` as `[prompt, mustContain, mustNotContain]`. A case with no group therefore serialises to the same string as on `main` and keeps its hash. At the head exactly one eval file under `skills/` carries the key, one occurrence: case 6. So one case re-keys and no other. The recordings agree: round A, run on `f0bbe3940e` with the new `hashCase` and main's tokens, carries `sha256:bd7f01e4b5bc2ac3…` on all 20 records; round B carries `sha256:b6390ca3b27f04dd…` on all 20. Right.
- `ui/scripts/check-skill-eval-tokens.mjs` (not in the diff) reads `must_contain` and `must_not_contain` only. Case 6 now counts under its printed "must_contain is EMPTY" tally, on which it takes no verdict, and the bundle still holds other `must_contain` tokens, so no precondition trips. Its check-run is green. Answered under ③.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/37928-skill-evals-any-of.md`: `@objectstack/scenarios` patch, `@objectstack/skills` patch. Both levels are right.

- `@objectstack/scenarios` publishes `dist`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`. Nothing under `src/` outside `src/skill-evals/` imports the runner, and its script runs from `src` through tsx, so of this package only the README ships a change. `Metadata-protocol: none` takes patch (AGENTS.md, Post-Task step 3).
- `@objectstack/skills` ships the `skills/**` tree whole, the eval file with it; a grading-token change with no protocol kind takes patch.
- Clause-②: no. Holds: no spec schema, no runtime accept-set and no published export moves; the eval JSON form is read by a checkout-only runner. The line is on the PR body and in the changeset body, both line-initial.
- Metadata-protocol: none. Holds: nothing a metadata author can write changes.

Sentence by sentence, against the tree:
- "a list of groups, each a list of tokens … every group is required … `[["a", "b"], ["c"]]` reads (a or b) and c": true (`gradeAnswer`: `filter` over groups, `some` over tokens).
- "a literal, case-sensitive substring, nothing normalised, no model judge": true (`answer.includes(t)`, the same call the other two forms use).
- "refuses a `must_contain_any` that is not a list of groups, a group that is empty or not a list of strings, a group holding an empty token, and a case with no token in any of the three forms": true (`anyOfProblem`, then the asserts-nothing sum).
- "A failing run record names each unmet group whole in `unmetAny` (the key is absent when every group is met), and the round summary prints it in the missed column": true; round B's with-skill r8 record and `summary.md` show both.
- "The runner runs from a checkout only; of `@objectstack/scenarios`, the published README is what changes": true.
- The hash paragraph: true, as ① reads it.
- The case 6 paragraph: true. Round A shows the misgrade it names (9 of 10 correct with-skill answers failed main's pair; 4 of the 10 are in Chinese). Prompt, `expected_output` and `must_not_contain` are unchanged in the diff, and `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` is not in it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none in the dev report.
- Deviation, the scratch driver. The CLI at the head has no per-case flag (`--skills`, `--repeats`, `--triggers-only` and the rest select bundles, never a case), so a single-case round cannot be asked of it. Accepted as a round of the runner for this card, on what the records themselves show: schema `skill-eval-run/1`, the runner's record keys, `caseHash` equal across each round, `bundlesLoaded` `objectstack-ai` on every with-skill turn and empty on every no-skill turn, no invalid or error turn, `summary.md` in the runner's own rendering, `round.json` naming sha `07fe4d2f…` and `dirty: false`. The verdicts are reproducible from the recorded answers alone: my literal count gives the same 9/10 and 0/10. What stays unseen is the driver's own code; `round.json` is the driver's shape, not the CLI's. See N3.
- Deviation, no case added under `packages/qa/scenarios/test/skill-evals/`: accepted. The card's acceptance names the self-test, and the self-test carries it.
- Out-of-scope note, `check-skill-eval-tokens.mjs` does not read `must_contain_any`: a follow-up, not a gap on this head. The gate sits outside the card's claimed surface and the card's four items do not name it. On this head nothing is untaught: all four tokens occur in `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` at the head, three of them in the approval paragraph itself (lines 163 to 167: "signed-in session", "`ai:approve` does not decide it", "is refused", "never decides them"). The shape checks the gate also skips are made by `cases.ts` when the catalog loads. But the dev left it "noted, not filed", with no carrier. See N2.
- Out-of-scope note, answers in Chinese on an English prompt: confirmed in the recordings (round A 4 of 10 with the skill and 7 of 10 without; round B 1 and 6). It bears on the English-phrase family of card item 4, not on this diff.
- Security. The one changed skills hunk moves the grading tokens of a case about an authentication and permission rule (an API token refused on the AI approval door; `ai:approve`). It teaches nothing new and the skill text is unchanged, but it decides which answers about that rule read as correct, so the line above reads `yes` and the low-risk arm does not apply. The card and the PR body already ask for the maintainer's approval of the eval file.
- SQL push-down: not applicable; the diff holds no query, no id materialisation and no join.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

**(a) The any-of form, card items 1 and 2.**
- `grade.ts`. Matching is `answer.includes(t)` inside `group.some`, the same literal, case-sensitive call as the all-of form; no lowercasing, trimming or regex, no model. `pass` now also needs `unmetAny.length === 0`. The unmet groups are copied (`[...group]`), whole, in the case's order, and the key is spread in only when non-empty. `mustContainAny = []` by default, so a caller passing the old two-list object grades as before. The jsdoc agrees with the code sentence by sentence.
- `cases.ts`. `anyOfProblem` refuses a value that is not an array (a string, an object, `null`: the destructuring default covers `undefined` only), a group that is not a list of strings, an empty group, and a group holding an empty token; each refusal carries the case's location and the group index. A case with no token in any form still refuses. A trigger case carrying `assertions` still refuses before any of this. `mustContainAny` is set on the parsed case only when there is a group. The header comment agrees.
- `hashCase`: as ① reads it. Includes the groups; re-keys only a case that carries them; token order and group order are part of the hash, which is the right side to err on.
- `run.ts`. `verdictOf` and `applyVerdict` carry `unmetAny` only when non-empty; `regradeRecord` strips a recorded `unmetAny` before re-applying the verdict, so a regrade cannot leave a stale one. `judgeTurn` passes the whole case to the grader, so the groups reach it with no further wiring. A changed case is still set apart and never regraded.
- `summary.ts`. Unmet groups of failing with-skill turns are collected whole and deduplicated by their serialised form; the per-case row prints them after the all-of tokens as `(none of: …)`, each token through the same `code` cell escaper the other columns use. Round B's `summary.md` shows the real thing.
- `README.md`: true in every changed sentence (the grading rule, the worked example, the two refusals it names, `unmetAny`, the hash sentence, the records sentence). It names two of the four malformed-shape refusals and does not claim the list is complete.

**(b) The self-test, against the card's acceptance.** Six new rows, floor 34 to 40, each registered in `SELF_TEST_BATTERIES`.
- A group met by its second token passes: row 1 swaps `$icontains` for `$endsWith`, the second token of `['$icontains', '$endsWith']`, and requires `pass` and no `unmetAny`. Covered.
- A group with none of its tokens fails: row 2 uses `$EndsWith`, a case-only difference, and requires FAIL with the group named whole and `missing` and `forbidden` empty. Covered, and it pins case-sensitivity for the new form as well.
- All-of and `must_not_contain` unchanged: row 3 shows each deciding alone beside a met group, plus a second unmet group failing; the five pre-existing grader rows are untouched in the diff. Covered.
- Beyond the card: seven malformed shapes refused and a groups-only case read; the group-less hash compared against the old formula computed inside the row, a group added or edited re-keying, and `--regrade` setting the earlier record apart; the summary rendering. The check-runs on the head are green, which is the gate verdict on these rows.

**(c) Case 6, card item 3.**
- Unchanged: the prompt, `expected_output`, and `must_not_contain` `["pendingActions.approve("]`. The hunk is one line, `must_contain` replaced by `must_contain_any`. No other case and no skill text moves.
- The four tokens are of the kind the card asks for: `ai:approve` is a code spelling (the permission name); `signed-in session`, `refused` and `never decides` are the refusal wording of the approval paragraph and of the reference answer. All four are in round A's with-skill answers (r1 carries all four).
- What each token caught, with-skill arm, by my count of the recordings:

| token | round A (of 10) | round B (of 10) | the only token in |
|:--|--:|--:|:--|
| `ai:approve` | 9 | 8 | A r8, A r10, B r3, all three in Chinese |
| `refused` | 3 | 8 | A r9, B r1 |
| `never decides` | 7 | 3 | none |
| `signed-in session` | 1 | 1 | none |

  No no-skill answer in either round carries any of the four (0 of 20). `ai:approve` is the member that survives a change of language; `refused` rescues one correct English answer per round that never names the permission; the other two decided nothing on these 20 turns and are specific enough to be harmless.
- The no-skill arm fails two ways, and the group is the only thing that catches the second. Ten of the 20 no-skill answers write `pendingActions.approve(` and fail on the forbidden token. The other ten write no script: they ask for the client's API first, propose alternatives, and offer to write approve-everything on the token if the user confirms. That is a wrong answer of the kind the case exists to catch, it carries no forbidden token, and it fails only because it holds none of the four.
- So is `refused` alone too loose? It is the weakest member, and the risk is real but narrow. The idea of refusing is in most of those ask-first answers already: eight of the Chinese ones write 拒绝 or 被拒, for "reject the stale items" or for the harness denying a read outside the work directory. The English ones happened to write "reject", "denied", "wasn't allowed"; one that had said "the read was refused" would have passed while offering to approve on a token. The nearest recorded miss is round B no-skill r1, "you've chosen to refuse automatic approval", one inflection away, and that answer fails on the forbidden token anyway. Measured, the looseness cost nothing: 0 of 20. The area's own example, an answer that approves through REST or another spelling and also says "refused", did not occur: no with-skill answer in either round contains `/approve` or any approve call, and their `fetch(` calls only list. The prompt pins `@objectstack/client`, and all ten no-skill script writers used the forbidden spelling.
- Against that, every with-skill use of `refused` in the recordings is the expected one (a token or call "is refused"), the card names "refusal terms" as an admissible kind, and dropping the token would turn two correct answers red (round A offline 9/10, round B 8/10, the bar's edge), which is the misgrade the ruling filed this card to remove. No tighter literal covers both rescued answers ("token are refused", "approval call refused"). I leave it in, as N1, with a condition for returning it.

**(d) Acceptance.**
- Round B is fresh and on the pushed head. `round.json`: sha `07fe4d2fa8773b97ee53443707e5fe37c20501de`, `dirty: false`, started 13:07:46Z, one minute after the head commit (13:06:45Z) and after round A ended (13:05:19Z). Its 20 answers share none with round A's 20. Round A is the token round, on `f0bbe3940e` with main's tokens. Round B reads 9/10 with the skill and 0/10 without, no invalid or error turn, one model on both arms; the bars are 8 or more and 2 or fewer. Met, with no retune. The one with-skill miss (r8) is a correct answer in the present tense ("refuses") that names no `ai:approve`; it is inside the bar and reported as measured.
- The scratch driver: counts, for the reasons under ③, with N3.
- `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` is not in the diff (8 files; the only path under `skills/` is the eval file, one line each way).
- The ratchet: `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` and its ceilings are not in the diff, so no ceiling is raised; the lint workflow runs it and every lint check-run on the head is success. `skills/NAME/evals/**` is its population 1b, measured and printed, unpriced: the eval file is measured, not ratcheted.

N1 (nit) — `refused` is the loosest member of case 6's group: an ordinary English word, and the group is the only assertion that fails an ask-first wrong answer. Left as an accepted deviation on the measured 0 of 20 and the card's own wording. If a later round shows a no-skill pass, or a with-skill pass of a wrong answer, carried by `refused` alone, the token returns to the decision box with that recording; it is not to be tuned silently.
N2 (nit) — the gate gap in `ui/scripts/check-skill-eval-tokens.mjs` (any-of tokens are neither shape-checked nor scored as taught, and a groups-only case is tallied as an empty `must_contain`) has no carrier. File the follow-up card before case 12 or the English-phrase family moves to the form; the dev's dedupe words are in report 7219513608.
N3 (nit) — a single-case round needed an uncommitted driver because the CLI has no per-case filter. A `--case` flag would make the next acceptance round a round of the committed runner, reviewable end to end. Follow-up, not this card.
N4 (nit) — the README and the changeset show the summary form as `(none of: a / b)`; the renderer puts each token in a code span. And the header comment of `cli.ts` (not in the diff) still names two assertion forms. Prose only.

## 席位核对

**Shape and gates.** 8 files, +185/-23. Check-runs at 07fe4d2f: 34 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed. Governed: the one path under `skills/**` is the case-6 eval line. `Clause-②: no` · `Metadata-protocol: none`.

**Contract review.** Record 7220167777 at this head: PASS, served at the contract tier (`verify-review-tier` PASS), four nits, nothing graded. I adopt it.

**Ratchet, measured by me.** I merged this head onto current `origin/main` in a scratch worktree and ran `node scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`. It exits 0. The eval file is measured (3420 tokens), not ratcheted. `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` is not in the diff, so the approval paragraph is untouched, as the ruling requires.

**The card's acceptance, row by row.**
- **Self-test.** A group met by its second token passes. A group with none of its tokens fails, and since the miss differs only in case it also pins case-sensitivity. All-of and `must_not_contain` are unchanged, and the five earlier grader rows are untouched.
- **Fresh round B on the pushed head.** `round.json` names `07fe4d2f` with `dirty: false`, and round B starts after round A ends with no answer shared. It scored 9/10 with the skill and 0/10 without, against bars of 8 or more and 2 or fewer. There was no retune, and the record re-derives both counts from the recorded answers.
- **Hash.** It re-keys case 6 only, because a case with no group serialises as on `main`. Both rounds' records carry one hash each.

**The area's question: is `refused` too loose?** It stays as an accepted deviation, N1 in the record. It is the weakest member, and the group is the only assertion that fails an ask-first wrong answer, so the worry is fair. Measured, though, none of the four tokens occurs in any of the 20 no-skill answers. Each with-skill use is the expected "is refused". Dropping it would turn two correct answers red (round B 8/10, the bar's edge), which is the misgrade this card exists to remove. The card names "refusal terms" as admissible. The condition is recorded: if a later round shows a pass carried by `refused` alone on a wrong answer, the token goes back to the decision box with that recording.

**The scratch driver: accepted as a round of the runner for this card.** The CLI has no per-case flag, and the records carry the runner's own schema, record keys and verdicts, which re-derive from the answers. N3 asks for a `--case` flag so the next acceptance round runs on the committed runner. That is a follow-up.

**Follow-ups to file**, none blocking:
- N2: `ui/scripts/check-skill-eval-tokens.mjs` does not read `must_contain_any`. All four tokens occur in the skill today, but this needs a carrier before case 12 or the English-phrase family moves to the form.
- N3: `--case` on the CLI.
- N4: prose in the README, the changeset and the `cli.ts` header.

**Changeset.** `@objectstack/scenarios` and `@objectstack/skills` patch are right. Every sentence matches the code, as the record walks through.
